title: Plans for the future and jazz as dance music
summary: He will work as leader or sideman wherever the money is, and insists jazz should be danceable.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well, we're just about getting down to the wire with this; this has been such a beautiful experience talking with you, Panama. But I'd like to ask you a couple of things.
You mentioned in January, you're going back to Europe with your own band. What is your future? What are you looking for your plans for the future in the music business? What are you looking towards?

Well, I tell you -- I consider myself, I usually look upon myself as a prostitute -- wherever the money is, that's where I'm going. If I can make money as a leader, I mean if someone wants me to -- I'm not going to put myself in the position where I would be asking someone, but if someone thought enough of me and had enough faith in me that they thought I could lead a band and thought I could do so, I'd be happy to do it.
And, if they want me to be a side man, I'd be happy
Is there any particular type of music you'd really choose for the future to play in any particular way?

Well, I still have maintained that jazz was primarily music to dance to, and I still hold on to that theory. I feel that people should be able to not only sit and listen to jazz, but they should be able to dance to it, also, if they so choose to do so. Because this is the way it used to be and this is the way this music, to me, was founded, ton. I feel the music was founded because the people had to have something to dance to, and that's how this music came about.
